region: Pommard · Côte de Beaune, Burgundy, France
about: Domaine Cyrot-Buthiau was founded in the 1920s by Paul-Joseph Cyrot, who learned his trade managing the Château de Pommard and later the Clos de Tart, then bought vines of his own in Pommard. His great-grandson Olivier Cyrot has run the estate since 1989, now with his brother Marc-Emmanuel. Their cellars are cut into a rocky escarpment in Pommard beside the premier cru Les Arvelets, and the family farms about six hectares from Pommard and Volnay south to Santenay and Maranges.

Pinot Noir from Pommard remains the heart of the domaine. The village Pommard is assembled from fifteen small plots totalling about three hectares across the appellation, a blend that evens out the differences between sites. In 2023 about 15% of the grapes were fermented as whole bunches, and the wine was aged in barrel with around 20% new oak, enough to frame the fruit without dominating it.

London merchant Corney & Barrow tasted the 2023 from barrel and found bright wild strawberry, then a generous, supple palate of black cherry, raspberry and a creamy note, with firm tannins coated in fruit and lively acidity. Look too for bramble, black currant, iron and fresh mint. Corney & Barrow suggest it will be at its best from around 2027 to 2030.
facts: 15 village plots, about 3 ha in Pommard
